meetings.title: Pricing tiers review

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay, let's get into pricing. The goal today is to lock the tiers so marketing can start on the launch page.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sure. Priya here. I've got the competitor sheet open. Most of them land between $15 and $20 for the individual plan.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Right, and we said the free plan stays. 3 meetings a week, transcripts only, no enhanced notes.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Marcus. I'd push for Pro at $18 a month. It's below Granola and it covers unlimited meetings and chat.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I agree with $18. For Team I'd do $30 per seat with shared folders and admin controls.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: $30 per seat feels right if SSO is included. Is SSO in Team or only Enterprise?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Team gets Google sign-in. Okta and SAML SSO stay Enterprise only. That's what Acme will need, by the way.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Fine. What about the annual discount?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: 20% off for annual billing. That's standard and finance is happy with it.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay, decision: Free stays, Pro at $18 a month, Team at $30 per seat, 20% annual discount.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: And the launch date? Marketing asked for at least three weeks.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Let's say November 15th for the pricing launch. Priya, can you own the pricing page copy?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yes, I'll have a draft of the pricing page by Friday the 9th.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I'll update Stripe with the new plans and test the upgrade flow. Should be done by the 20th.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Great. One open question is students. Do we do a student discount?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Let's park it. We don't have data on students yet.

meetings.enhancedNotes:
## Tiers
- Free stays: three meetings a week, transcripts only, no enhanced notes (0:22)
- Pro at $18/month with unlimited meetings and chat (0:30)
- Team at $30 per seat with shared folders and admin controls (0:38)
- Okta and SAML SSO are Enterprise only; Team gets Google sign-in (0:53)

## Annual discount
- 20% off annual billing (1:06)

## Launch date
- Pricing launch on November 15 (1:25)

## Action items
- Priya: pricing page draft by Friday, October 9 (1:33)
- Marcus: new plans in Stripe and upgrade flow tested by October 20 (1:39)

## Open questions
- Student discount — parked until there is data (1:53)

meetings.title: Acme onboarding kickoff

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Thanks for making the time, Janet. Let's walk through the rollout plan for Acme.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Happy to. So we're planning to start with the sales team, that's about 120 seats.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: 120 seats on the Team plan, okay. Any hard requirements before rollout?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Two. First, SSO through Okta is non-negotiable. Security won't approve anything without it. We need it by December 1st.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Understood. Okta SSO is on our Enterprise plan and we're finishing the integration now.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Second is data residency. Our legal team wants customer data kept in the EU. Is that possible?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Honestly, today everything is stored on the user's own Mac, so meeting content never leaves the device. Account data sits in the US right now.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: That helps a lot. Legal will still ask about account data. Can you put that in writing?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yes, I'll send a data handling document by next Wednesday.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Great. On budget, we've set aside $40,000 for the first year.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That works with 120 seats on annual billing. I'll send a formal quote.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Also my counterpart in IT is Raj Mehta. He'll handle the Okta side.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Perfect. Next step is an SSO check-in in about two weeks once Raj has the sandbox.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Sounds good. Let's do the 20th.

meetings.enhancedNotes:
## Account
- Acme starts with the sales team, about 120 seats (0:10)
- First-year budget is $40,000 (1:09)

## Requirements
- Okta SSO is non-negotiable, needed by December 1 (0:23)
- Legal wants customer data kept in the EU (0:38)
- Meeting content stays on each Mac; account data is in the US today (0:46)

## Contacts
- Raj Mehta in IT owns the Okta side (1:21)

## Next steps
- Send data handling document by next Wednesday (1:04)
- Send formal quote for 120 seats on annual billing (1:15)
- SSO check-in on October 20 (1:34)

meetings.title: Backend engineer debrief: Sam Okafor
meetings.roughNotes:
- sam okafor
- strengths / concerns
- next step

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay, debrief for Sam Okafor, the backend candidate. Leo, you did the Postgres round?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yeah. Sam was excellent on Postgres. Query plans, indexing, he spotted the missing index in about two minutes.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Dana here. The system design round was weaker. He designed the sync service without thinking about offline clients until I prompted him.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Was it a gap in knowledge or just nerves?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Probably nerves. Once I pointed it out he came up with a decent conflict resolution approach.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Culture and communication?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Really good. Clear communicator and he asked sharp questions about how we keep everything local.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. My read is strong yes on technical depth, small concern on system design. Let's move him to the final round.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Agreed. For the final round let's do a deeper system design session with Marcus.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: And for the offer band, we budgeted $165,000 to $180,000 for this role.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: If he does well in the final, I'd go toward the top of the band. Competing offers are likely.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Decision: Sam moves to the final round, system design with Marcus. Leo, can you schedule it?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yes, I'll get it on the calendar for the week of the 19th.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Morning everyone. Quick round. Marcus?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Stripe plans are in test mode. The upgrade flow works, downgrade has a proration bug I'm fixing today.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Priya?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Pricing page draft is done and in review. Also heads up, I'm out this Friday.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Leo?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Working on the Okta SSO integration. I'm blocked on the Okta sandbox, Acme's IT hasn't sent credentials yet.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: I'll ping Janet and Raj Mehta about the sandbox today.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Dana here. Release 2.4 is slipping. The transcript export bug is bigger than we thought. New target is October 22nd.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay, 2.4 moves to the 22nd. Anything else blocking?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Nope, that's it.

meetings.title: Pricing follow-up

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: We're revisiting pricing because of the churn data Marcus pulled. Marcus, go ahead.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: So in the beta survey, users who'd pay at $18 churned about twice as fast as users at $15. $16 looks like the sweet spot.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: So the proposal is Pro at $16 instead of $18?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yes. Team stays at $30 per seat. That part tested fine.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Priya. If Pro drops to $16 I'd also bump the annual discount to 25% to push people onto annual plans.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Finance okay with 25%?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: They said yes as long as annual is at least 40% of new signups.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay, new decision: Pro is $16 a month, Team stays $30 per seat, annual discount goes to 25%.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: That means the pricing page needs another pass and Stripe needs updating. Can we move the launch?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Let's move the pricing launch from November 15th to November 20th to be safe.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I'll update the pricing page copy by Monday.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: And I'll change the Stripe prices and fix the proration bug by Friday.

meetings.enhancedNotes:
## Churn data
- Beta users at $18 churned about twice as fast as at $15; $16 is the sweet spot (0:10)

## Decision
- Pro is now $16/month (was $18) (0:51)
- Team stays at $30 per seat (0:26)
- Annual discount rises to 25% (was 20%) (0:31)
- Finance condition: annual must be at least 40% of new signups (0:44)

## Launch
- Pricing launch moves from November 15 to November 20 (1:06)

## Action items
- Priya: pricing page copy by Monday (1:13)
- Marcus: Stripe prices and proration fix by Friday (1:17)

meetings.title: 1:1 with Dana

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: How are things going, Dana?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Mostly good. Busy with 2.4. But I wanted to talk about what's next for me.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Sure, go for it.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I'd really like to lead the mobile app team when we start it next year. I built the iOS prototype on my own time.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: I saw that, it's impressive. Leading mobile is realistic. Let's build a promotion case to senior engineer for Q1.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: That would be great. The other thing is on-call. I've been on call three of the last four weeks.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That's not okay. Let's move to a weekly rotation across the whole team starting next Monday.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Thank you. Also, could I get budget for the Swift conference in March?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yes, approved. Book it and expense it, up to $2,000 including travel.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Perfect, thanks.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: I'll draft the promotion case outline by the end of the month and we'll go through it together.

meetings.roughNotes:

- EU data

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Hi Janet, hi Raj. Let's start with SSO. Leo says the Okta integration is working in staging now.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Raj here. Yes, we tested it yesterday with 10 users. Login works, and group sync works too.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Great. Anything left before December 1st?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Just SCIM deprovisioning. When someone leaves Acme, their seat should be removed automatically.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Leo can have SCIM deprovisioning done by November 10th.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Janet. Legal read the data handling document, thank you. They're fine with meeting content staying on the Mac.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: But they still want account data in the EU. Is there a timeline?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: We'll have a Frankfurt region for account data by January. I can put that in the contract.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: That works. One more thing. With the new pricing, can we get a discount for 120 seats?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: We can do 10% off the first year if the contract is signed by November 30th.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I think we can make that. I'll take it to procurement this week.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Great. I'll send the updated quote with the 10% and the Frankfurt commitment.

segments.text: January 14th to 16th works for everyone except Marcus, who lands on the 15th.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: That's fine. January 14th to 16th in Lisbon. How many people?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: 18 including the 2 new hires, assuming Sam Okafor accepts.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Budget?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Finance approved $25,000 total, flights included.

segments.speaker: me

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I'll book the venue by November 1st.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: I'll draft the agenda. Day one roadmap, day two mobile app kickoff, day three is free.

meetings.title: Sam Okafor final round

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Final round debrief for Sam Okafor. Marcus, how did system design go?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Much better than the first time. He designed the sync service with offline clients from the start and talked through conflict resolution clearly.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: So the concern from the first round is resolved?

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Yes, I'd say so. Strong hire.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Leo. Agreed. And he mentioned he has a competing offer from a fintech company.

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Okay. Let's make the offer at the top of the band. $175,000 base.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Can we do $175,000 plus the standard equity grant?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: Yes, $175,000 base plus standard equity. I'll send the offer today.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Start date?

segments.speaker: me
segments.text: He asked for December 2nd. That's fine.

segments.speaker: them
segments.text: Great, I'll start the onboarding checklist and get his laptop ordered.
